main_text.head: De servili cognatione. Von leibeigener knechtlicher Sippschafft.

head.i: Quid dicit Imperator de servili successione?

main_text.p: Concessimus, inquit, ut si quis in servili constitutus consortio, liberum vel liberos habuerit, sive ex libera, sive ex servilis cōditionis muliere: vel contra serva mulier ex libero vel servo habuerit liberos cujuscunq; sexus: Et ad libertatem his pervenientibus, ij, qui ex servili ventre nati sunt, libertatem meruerint, vel dum mulieres liberae erant, ipsi in servitute eos habuerint, & postea ad libertatem pervenerint: ut hi omnes ad successionem patris vel matris veniant, patronatus jure in hac parte sopito. in princ. inst. eod.

head.i: Estne pronepos defuncti potior, quàm defuncti frater aut pater?

main_text.p: Cùm prima causa sit suorum haeredum, & eorum, quos inter suos haeredes enumeravimus: apparet pronepotem & abnepotem defuncti potiorem esse, quàm fratrem aut patrem matremq; defuncti, inquit Imperator, §. repetitis. inst. cod.

page.notes: Printed flourishes after "Quinta Regula" and "Titulus" are read as "?" but may be ornaments; the "?" marks are uncertain. The German title is in black letter and is marked with bl. The heading "QUIS EST SEPTIMUS" is set in italic capitals. A decorative rule divides the Quinta Regula paragraph from the title; it is not text. Initial "C" of the paragraph beginning "Concessimus" is a large letter joined to the word.
